nodes.name: Heat-assisted phosphating of Co-SeMON
nodes.procedure: The metal-organic nanosheet precursors Co-SeMON and the Se-free counterpart Co-MON were synthesized according to our previous work (Figure S1). Subsequently, Se-doped CoP was synthesized through a heat-assisted phosphating treatment of the Co-SeMON precursors (Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanoflower-like morphology of interconnected 2D nanosheets for Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b) of Se-CoP show the nanoflower-like morphology composed of interconnected 2D nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows average thicknesses of Se-CoP and CoP nanosheets are 4.4±0.1 nm and 4.5±0.1 nm, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average thicknesses of Se-CoP and CoP nanosheets are ca. 4.4±0.1 and 4.5±0.1 nm, respectively, as evidenced by the atomic force microscopy (AFM) images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Se-CoP possesses BET specific surface area of 21 m² g⁻¹ and highly mesoporous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Se-CoP possesses a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area of 21 m² g⁻¹ and a highly mesoporous structure (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping proves uniform distribution of Co, P, and Se elements in Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images (Figure 1d) prove that the presence and uniform distribution of Co, P, and Se elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES verifies Co, P, and Se contents in Se-CoP as 26.6, 25.8, and 14.3 wt%, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) and element analysis verify that the Co, P, and Se elements in Se-CoP are 26.6, 25.8, and 14.3 wt%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM identifies lattice fringes of 0.249 and 0.187 nm corresponding to (111) and (211) planes of orthorhombic CoP in Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1e) clearly identifies the lattice fringes of 0.249 and 0.187 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (211) crystal planes of orthorhombic CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD patterns of Se-CoP and CoP confirm orthorhombic CoP crystal phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns (Figure 1f) of both Se-CoP and CoP further confirm this crystal phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 peaks at 778.7 and 792.9 eV for Co-P bond in Se-CoP with 0.4 eV positive shift vs CoP; Se 3d5/2 and Se 3d3/2 at 55.4 and 56.2 eV confirm lattice Se incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the high-resolution Co 2p spectra of Se-CoP and CoP (Figures S6a and S7a), the binding energies of Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 exhibit characteristic peaks at 778.7 and 792.9 eV... As for Se 3d spectrum of Se-CoP (Figure S6c), the two peaks fitted at 55.4 and 56.2 eV originate from the binding energies of Se 3d5/2 and Se 3d3/2 in Co-Se bond, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA indicates Se-CoP exhibits excellent thermal stability in inert atmosphere.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) indicates that Se-CoP exhibits excellent thermal stability in an inert atmosphere (Figure S5).
